questions.q: Which command lists the files and directories in the current directory?
questions.e: `ls` lists directory contents. `pwd` prints the working directory, `ps` lists processes and `cd` changes directory.

questions.q: Which command prints the absolute path of the current working directory?
questions.e: `pwd` stands for print working directory and shows the full path of where you are.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Linux file system hierarchy.
I. System-wide configuration files are mainly stored in `/etc`.
II. User home directories are stored in `/bin`.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only I is correct. `/etc` holds configuration files such as passwd and fstab. `/bin` holds essential commands, and home directories are under `/home`.

questions.q: Which command is used to search for lines matching a pattern in a file?
questions.e: `grep pattern file` prints the lines that match the pattern.

questions.q: The program that reads commands typed by the user and passes them to the kernel for execution is called the ______.
questions.e: The shell (bash, sh, ksh) is the command interpreter between the user and the kernel.

questions.q: In the vi editor, which key is pressed to return from insert mode to command mode?
questions.e: Pressing Esc leaves insert mode and returns vi to command (normal) mode.

questions.q: Which command displays the manual page of a given command?
questions.e: `man ls` shows the manual page for ls. `which` shows the path of a command and `who` lists logged-in users.

questions.q: Which command displays the currently running processes of the user's session?
questions.e: `ps` reports a snapshot of current processes. `df` and `du` report disk space.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT stored as a field in each line of the `/etc/passwd` file?
o: Disk space used by the user
questions.e: Each line of `/etc/passwd` has the login name, UID, GID, comment, home directory and login shell. Disk usage is not recorded there.

questions.q: What is printed by `echo "red green blue" | awk '{print $2}'`?
questions.e: awk splits the line on whitespace into fields; `$2` is the second field, which is green.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about quoting in the shell.
I. Variables are expanded inside single quotes.
II. Variables are not expanded inside double quotes.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. Single quotes stop expansion, so `'Hello $name'` prints the text as it is. Double quotes allow variable expansion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about redirection in the shell.
I. The operator `>` overwrites the existing content of the target file.
II. The operator `>>` appends the output to the end of the target file.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: `>` truncates and writes a fresh file while `>>` appends. Both statements are correct.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT stored in the inode of a file?
questions.e: An inode keeps metadata and block pointers; the file name is stored in the directory entry that maps the name to the inode number.

questions.q: In the System V init scheme, which of the following runlevel descriptions is NOT correct?
questions.e: Runlevel 6 reboots the system, while runlevel 0 halts it. Runlevel 1 is single-user mode and runlevel 3 is multi-user text mode.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disk-related commands.
I. `df` reports the free and used space of mounted file systems.
II. `du` reports the space used by files and directories.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. `df` summarises space per file system, while `du` measures the usage of particular files and directories.

questions.q:
Regarding file ownership and permissions, consider the following statements.
I. `chown` changes the permission bits of a file.
II. `chmod` changes the permission bits of a file.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. `chmod` changes the permission bits, whereas `chown` changes the owner of a file.

questions.q: If the umask is 022, the default permissions of a newly created regular file are ______.
questions.e: Files start from 666 and the umask bits are removed: 666 − 022 = 644. Directories start from 777 and become 755.

questions.q: What is the output of `echo banana | sed 's/a/o/g'`?
questions.e: The g flag replaces every occurrence of a with o on the line, giving bonono. Without g only the first a would change, giving bonana.

questions.q: A file shows the permissions `-rwsr-xr-x` in the output of `ls -l`. The equivalent octal mode is ______.
questions.e: The s in the owner execute position is the setuid bit, which is the leading 4. Owner rwx = 7, group r-x = 5, others r-x = 5.

questions.q: The file `data.txt` contains five lines: one, two, three, four, five (one per line). What does `head -n 4 data.txt | tail -n 2` print?
o: four and five, on two lines
three and four, on two lines
one and two, on two lines
questions.e: `head -n 4` outputs the first four lines (one to four). `tail -n 2` keeps the last two of these: three and four.
